title: Performance basics and avoiding unnecessary work
learningObjectives: Explain performance basics and avoiding unnecessary work and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: Performance depends on JavaScript execution, network requests, DOM size, rendering, layout, and memory. Avoid unnecessary repeated work, batch DOM updates, debounce expensive input handlers where appropriate, lazy-load non-critical resources, and measure before optimising.
understand.whyItMatters: Performance affects responsiveness, battery use, and access on slower devices. Measurement helps distinguish real bottlenecks from assumptions.
understand.analogy: Performance work is like finding the actual queue causing a delay instead of speeding up a step that was already fast.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The handler waits briefly after typing stops before running the search. A production app should also cancel stale network requests when appropriate.

examples.explanation: The handler waits briefly after typing stops before running the search. A production app should also cancel stale network requests when appropriate.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Measure a page interaction, identify the costly work, and apply one targeted improvement. Record before-and-after measurements.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: What should guide a performance optimisation?
questions.explanation: Measure representative behaviour before changing code for performance.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
